title: Why S-Traps Fail: Understanding Trap Siphonage
description: An unvented S-trap creates a self-siphonage effect when water discharges rapidly down the vertical drop. As liquid rushes through the vertical pipe, it creates a negative pressure zone that pulls the protective water seal out of the trap dip. Without air introduced by a vent, sewer gases can freely enter the living space. Replacing legacy S-traps with a properly vented P-trap maintains the liquid barrier by allowing atmospheric air pressure to equalize during discharge. Always consult local plumbing codes for minimum fixture drain arm lengths before dropping vertically into a stack.
